newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown hikes stamp duty, cuts MIRAS.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown hikes stamp duty, cuts MIRAS.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown announced on Wednesday that he was cutting mortgage interest relief at source (MIRAS) to 10 percent as of April 1998, from the current level of 15.

He also announced he was raising stamp duty to 1.5 percent from one percent on property sales above 250,000 stg and and to two percent above 500,000 stg. These measures will take immediate effect after parliament passes the budget resolution.
"I will not allow house prices to get out of control and put at risk the sustainability of the recovery," Brown told parliament.

MIRAS is currently available on he first 30,000 stg of a mortgage. Reducing MIRAS to 10 percent should garner some 900 million stg for the Treasury, at a cost to each of Britain's 10 million homeowners of up to 10 stg per month.
The recent strength of economic and housing market data are believed to have sparked Brown's decision to target the housing market, in a bid to head off an unsustainable economic boom.
